messages:
alex_support: Heads-up — customer acme-eu opened a SEV2. They pinned model traffic to eu-west-1 but our audit logs show requests routed to us-east-1 during a failover window. Compliance got pinged.
incidents-bot: alert AUDIT-RESIDENCY-1918765432 created (policy_violation).
maria_customer: we received a compliance email saying data left EU. this is blocking our deployment. pls advise.
ian_sre: Copying logs from router for the window 2026-07-14T03:12:10Z - 03:14:02Z:
```
{"req_id":"r-0a1b2c","project":"acme-eu","policy":"eu_only","preferred_region":"eu-west-1","chosen_region":"us-east-1","decision":"fallback_due_to_capacity","kv_cache_hit":false}
{"req_id":"r-0a1b2d","project":"acme-eu","policy":"eu_only","preferred_region":"eu-west-1","chosen_region":"us-east-1","decision":"fallback_due_to_capacity","reason":"routing_pool_shortage","trace":"route_selector.v2 -> fallback_path"}
```
alex_support: The router shows `decision":"fallback_due_to_capacity"` even though project has residency pin. looks like the residency-check ran after routing decision.
jen_ops: I saw a routing change rolled 2026-07-14T03:11Z that tweaked failover scoring. Reverting now to 2026-07-14T03:10Z config.
ian_sre: Repro steps I used locally:
1) export REDWOOD_PROJECT=acme-eu
2) curl -v -H "X-Redwood-Prefer-Region: eu-west-1" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
Expected: routed to eu-west-1 and residency_check=pass
Observed: routed to us-east-1 and audit flagged residency_check=fail
(Logs attached above)
elaine_legal: Please preserve all logs and DO NOT delete/rotate keys for this project until we finish the compliance review. We may need a written timeline for the regulator.
tyler_billing: Also flagging billing — if egress/cross-region pricing applied we need to issue credit hold for the window. Ticket #BILL-776 created.
jen_ops: Temporary mitigation: disabled cross-region fallback for projects with `residency_pin=true` at 03:18Z. That should stop further cross-region routing while we investigate.
alex_support: Customer notified that we paused cross-region fallback and are investigating.
ian_sre: Root cause hypothesis: route selection v2 starts fallback scoring before residency policy lookup completes under high control-plane load, so fallback path can be picked and only later residency fails but too late to prevent routing. Need to flip ordering so residency guard runs pre-routing.
elaine_legal: Outline required for regulator: timeline of events, list of requests routed out of region, mitigation steps, and confirmation when cross-region flow is blocked. Can ops compile by EOD?
jen_ops: I'll compile request list from audit-index between 03:12:00 and 03:19:00 and push to S3 (s3://redwood-incident-exports/1918765432/).
ian_sre: PR to enforce residency-first check opened: https://git.internal/redwood/routing/pull/482 (WIP). Will add test that simulates control-plane delay.
alex_support: Action items: 1) jen confirm export link 2) ian finalize PR and schedule hotfix 3) tyler prepare credit proposal 4) elaine keep regulator thread updated.
incidents-bot: Incident state changed -> investigation (assigned: ian_sre, jen_ops).
maria_customer: thanks — please keep us updated. compliance team is on call.
jen_ops: Export uploaded: s3://redwood-incident-exports/1918765432/audit-log.json (permissions: legal + SRE).
ian_sre: Hotfix scheduled at 04:10Z to alter check ordering + add end-to-end test. Rolling canary first, then full.
elaine_legal: Received export. preparing regulator timeline. thanks.
alex_support: Closing loop with customer after hotfix verification and billing credit. Will update once canary shows no cross-region routes for pinned projects.
incidents-bot: Alert AUDIT-RESIDENCY-1918765432 auto-acknowledged after mitigation.
